subject: general
question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Have people rolling in the aisles

options.text: To use false promises to pull people on one’s side
To have a dispute with someone

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"have people rolling in the aisles"** is used to describe a situation where something or someone is extremely funny, making an audience laugh uncontrollably.(लोगों को बहुत हँसाना)
 
• The **phrase likely originates** from the physical act of laughing so hard that you might roll side to side, as if you were in the aisles of a theater. 
 
• **Make an audience laugh uncontrollably**(दर्शकों को अनियंत्रित रूप से हँसाना): This option is the correct choice. It exactly matches the meaning of the idiom "have people rolling in the aisles".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'Make an audience laugh uncontrollably'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's examine the given options:
 
 
• **To use false promises to pull people on one’s side:** This option refers to manipulation or deceit in order to win someone's support or allegiance.(झूठे वादे करके लोगों को अपनी ओर खींचना)
 
• **To have a dispute with someone:** This option suggests having a disagreement or argument with someone. (किसी के साथ विवाद करना)
 
• **Willing to do something immediately:** This phrase refers to being eager or ready to take immediate action(तुरंत कुछ करने के लिए तत्पर)
